title: Synthetic qualifier and actor fidelity instrument - test material only
provenance: LCSP-360 synthetic qualifier and actor fidelity regression; not a real government instrument

provisions.content: Definitions. A covered service stores customer-created records and offers them to customers through a digital interface. The operator is the entity controlling that service. A portable copy contains all customer-created records in an interoperable machine-readable format. These definitions apply to SEM-002 through SEM-007.
Direct duty. The operator of a covered service must provide a portable copy to a requesting customer within seven calendar days after receiving the request.

Qualified prohibition. The operator must not impose commercial charges or technical obstacles intended to prevent a customer moving their customer-created records to another service. For both commercial charges and technical obstacles, the prohibition is limited to those intended to prevent that portability; this provision does not prohibit charges generally. The narrowly limited security exception in SEM-007 applies.

Conditional remedy. If failure to perform SEM-002 causes a customer documented financial loss, the operator must compensate that customer for the documented loss within thirty calendar days after receiving notice of that loss. Maintaining a compensation policy alone does not perform this payment duty.

Transition. This instrument takes effect on 1 January 2026. For covered services already operating before that date, the duties in SEM-002 and SEM-003 become applicable on 1 July 2026 after a six-month transition. For services first operating on or after 1 January 2026, those duties apply immediately on first operation.

Incorporation. When an operator delegates fulfilment of export requests to an external export provider, that provider must perform the portable-copy duty in SEM-002, with the same seven-day period and the definitions in SEM-001. Delegation does not remove the operator's own duty. This provision incorporates the operative duty rather than merely referring to its citation.

Limited exception. The operator may temporarily block a transfer prohibited from obstruction by SEM-003 only while a documented, specific security threat makes that transfer unsafe. The block must be proportionate to that threat and end when the threat ends. This exception does not remove or delay the portable-copy duty in SEM-002.

Directional roles for delegated fulfillment. Actor A is the covered-service operator and remains the legal holder of the portable-copy duty under SEM-002. Actor B is the external export provider performing fulfillment under SEM-006. The triggering condition is that Actor A delegates export-request fulfillment to Actor B, for the requesting customer and the customer-created records. Actor A is the delegator; Actor B is the fulfillment delegate, not the delegator. Actor A remains responsible for SEM-002 after delegation. Actor B's express SEM-006 performance duty remains distinct and does not transfer or replace Actor A's SEM-002 duty. Delegation by Actor B to Actor A is not the condition established by this provision.
